items.stem: A common delegation failure is handing over a task but not the matching authority. Why is that a problem?

options.text: The person is accountable for the outcome but cannot make the decisions needed to deliver it
options.rationale: Correct: responsibility without authority stalls the work and frustrates the owner.

options.text: It makes the task finish faster
options.rationale: It typically slows the work down.
Matching authority to the task is central to delegation.

options.text: It removes all need for check-ins
options.rationale: Check-ins are still needed; the issue is missing authority.

items.explanation: Correct: responsibility without authority stalls the work and frustrates the owner.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO describe healthy follow-through on a delegated task? (Select TWO)

options.text: Agreeing check-in points proportionate to the risk and the person's readiness
options.rationale: Correct: right-sized check-ins give support without micromanaging.

options.text: Course-correcting through questions rather than taking the task back
options.rationale: Correct: coaching the owner preserves ownership while fixing course.

options.text: Reviewing every small step the person takes
options.rationale: That is micromanaging and undermines ownership.

options.text: Ignoring the task entirely until the deadline
options.rationale: Abandonment is as harmful as micromanaging.

items.explanation: Correct: right-sized check-ins give support without micromanaging.

items.stem: What is the difference between accountability and responsibility in delegation?

options.text: Accountability is ultimate ownership of the outcome; responsibility is doing the work to deliver it
options.rationale: Correct: one person is accountable for the outcome even when work is shared as responsibility.

options.text: They are two words for exactly the same thing
options.rationale: They differ: ownership of outcome vs doing the work.
Responsibility for tasks is routinely delegated.

items.explanation: Correct: one person is accountable for the outcome even when work is shared as responsibility.
